speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. To help narrow down the cause of your dizziness and vertigo, how long does each episode typically last, and do you experience any hearing loss, tinnitus, or ringing in your ears?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail; the position-dependent nature of your episodes strongly suggests a benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV). To confirm this, have you noticed any specific head movements, like rolling in bed or looking up, that consistently trigger these spells? Additionally, do you experience any neck pain or stiffness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

Given the classic presentation of position-dependent vertigo in a 70-year-old without auditory symptoms or neurological deficits, the diagnosis is highly likely. I recommend performing the Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm the diagnosis and identify the affected canal.
